review.summary: The ordinance likely conflicts with current state ADU law (Gov. Code §§ 66310-66342) in 16 places. Main problems: it cites repealed § 65852.2 and related sections, requires owner occupancy and deed restrictions for ADUs, uses the 2018 unpermitted-ADU date, caps multifamily detached ADUs at two, and sets impact-fee, parking, setback, architecture and historic standards that go beyond state limits. It also appears to omit the 15-business-day completeness determination and the appeal process (§ 66317(a)(2), (d)). Items not covered by loaded sources (septic percolation test E.6, shared-driveway rule F.6, ADU permit fee D.2.b) are unclear. This is a screening aid, not legal advice. Check the live code, since the city may have amended it.

issues.rule: § 17.28.270(A) (also D.1.a.iv, E.5, E.8.a, G.2.a.ii): says the section is meant to comply with Gov. Code §§ 65852.2 and 65852.22 and cites § 65852.26.
issues.conflict: Those sections were renumbered by SB 477 and are no longer current law. The ordinance likely needs to cite and track §§ 66310-66342, including § 66342 for optional condominium conveyance.
issues.quote: updated from 65852.2, 65852.22, 65852.23, and 65852.26 to Government Code sections 66310-66342

issues.rule: § 17.28.270(D.1.d): allows 'no more than two detached ADUs' on a lot with an existing or proposed multifamily dwelling.
issues.conflict: State law allows up to two on a proposed multifamily dwelling but up to eight on an existing one, not to exceed the number of existing units. The two-unit cap on existing multifamily lots likely conflicts.
issues.quote: up to eight detached ADUs are allowed on a lot with an existing multifamily dwelling, not to exceed the number of existing units on the lot

issues.rule: § 17.28.270(D.4.a.i): no impact fee only for an ADU 'less than 750 square feet in size'; also silent on JADUs.
issues.conflict: State law exempts ADUs of 750 square feet of interior livable space or less (and JADUs of 500 or less). The ordinance would allow fees on a unit of exactly 750 square feet and does not state the JADU exemption.
issues.quote: if it contains 750 square feet of interior livable space or less

issues.rule: § 17.28.270(D.4.a.ii): impact fees apply to an ADU 'that is 750 square feet or larger'.
issues.conflict: State law applies proportional fees only to ADUs larger than 750 square feet of interior livable space. Charging at exactly 750 square feet likely conflicts.
issues.quote: If an ADU contains greater than 750 square feet of interior livable space, impact fees shall be charged proportionately

issues.rule: § 17.28.270(E.7.b): ADUs permitted on or after Jan. 1, 2025 are subject to an owner-occupancy requirement.
issues.conflict: State law bars owner-occupancy requirements for ADUs, with a narrow exception for certain qualified-buyer sales under § 66341. The ordinance imposes it generally.
issues.quote: instead mandates no owner-occupancy requirement for ADUs

issues.rule: § 17.28.270(E.7.c): all JADUs are subject to owner occupancy.
issues.conflict: State law requires owner occupancy only when the JADU shares sanitation facilities with the primary structure. JADUs with their own bathroom cannot be required to have it.
issues.quote: If the JADU does not have shared sanitation facilities, owner occupancy will not be required

issues.rule: § 17.28.270(E.8): requires a recorded deed restriction (no separate sale, size limits, enforcement, removal process) for every ADU and JADU before building permit issuance.
issues.conflict: The Handbook says a local agency cannot impose a deed restriction on an ADU. It allows a JADU deed restriction only for the no-separate-sale and size/attribute terms, so the added enforcement terms for JADUs may also go too far.
issues.quote: A local agency cannot impose a deed restriction on an ADU.

issues.rule: § 17.28.270(F.2.a): one off-street parking space is required for each ADU.
issues.conflict: State law caps parking at one space per unit or per bedroom, whichever is less. A studio or efficiency unit with no bedroom likely cannot be required to provide a space.
issues.quote: Parking requirements for ADUs shall not exceed one parking space per unit or bedroom, whichever is less

issues.rule: § 17.28.270(F.2.b): replacement parking is not required only when a 'garage, carport, or other covered parking structure' is demolished or converted.
issues.conflict: State law also covers uncovered off-street spaces. Omitting them could be read to allow replacement requirements for uncovered spaces.
issues.quote: may not require off-street parking spaces to be replaced when a garage, carport, covered parking structure, or uncovered parking space is demolished

issues.rule: § 17.28.270(F.2.c.v): the car-share parking exception applies only to a 'city-sanctioned, posted car-share pick-up or drop-off location' within one block.
issues.conflict: State law exempts the ADU whenever a car share vehicle is located within one block. The city's added 'sanctioned, posted' condition narrows the exemption.
issues.quote: When there is a car share vehicle located within one block of the ADU.

issues.rule: § 17.28.270(F.3.c): a detached ADU must be at least five feet from the primary building.
issues.conflict: State law says minimum separation requirements may not be applied if they unreasonably restrict ADUs unless required by the Building or Fire Code. The five-foot rule has no 800-square-foot safeguard like the one in F.4.c.
issues.quote: Minimum distance or other requirements may not be applied if they would unreasonably restrict the creation of ADUs

issues.rule: § 17.28.270(F.3.d): no setback only if the ADU is in the same location and dimensions as an 'existing accessory building'.
issues.conflict: State law waives setbacks for ADUs created within an existing living area or accessory structure, or in a new structure in the same location and dimensions as any existing structure. The ordinance is narrower.
issues.quote: No setback shall be required for an ADU or JADU created within an existing living area or accessory structure

issues.rule: § 17.28.270(F.7.a): exterior materials and colors must 'match the appearance and architectural design' of the primary dwelling.
issues.conflict: Matching appearance and design appears to call for personal judgment. The Handbook lists similar 'architecture style' language as subjective, and only objective standards may be applied to ADUs.

issues.rule: § 17.28.270(F.8): an ADU on or within 600 feet of a California Register property must not be visible from any public right-of-way.
issues.conflict: State law allows standards that prevent adverse impacts on listed properties. A flat no-visibility rule that reaches neighboring lots likely goes beyond that and may unreasonably restrict ADUs.
issues.quote: standards that prevent adverse impacts on any real property that is listed in the California Register of Historical Resources

issues.rule: § 17.28.270(G.2): protects unpermitted ADUs only if built before January 1, 2018, and cites § 65852.2.
issues.conflict: The cutoff is now January 1, 2020 under § 66311.7, so ADUs built in 2018-2019 are likely left unprotected. The repealed section is also cited.
issues.quote: Changes the date from January 1, 2018, to January 1, 2020

issues.rule: § 17.28.270(H): an ADU that does not meet the objective standards may be allowed through a discretionary Architectural Permit.
issues.conflict: State law requires a ministerial-only approval process for ADU applications. Sending applicants into a discretionary architectural review appears inconsistent, even if framed as optional.
issues.quote: Local agencies must provide an approval process that only includes ministerial provisions for the approval of ADU permit applications.
